text.p: Following are the highlights of main stories in Serbian and Montenegrin papers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
POLITIKA
- Serbian Development Fund allocates another 77 million German marks worth of credits to 62 export firms. So far loans worth 800 million marks granted for export-oriented production.
- Yugoslav airlines JAT restores flights to Egypt after five years.
- Beogradska banka AD 682nd on list of 1,000 biggest banks in the world, according to London magazine Banker.
- Federal Commodity Reserve Agency ready to buy 15,000 tonnes of new wheat to form commodity reserves and maintain market stability; auctions began on Monday.
- Yugoslavia has more than seven million registered voters, 70 percent of whom in Serbia.
- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic announces forming of own party for the forthcoming early parliamentary elections in the Bosnian Serb Republic which she has set for October 12.
- Only 2,000 refugees from Yugoslavia have returned to Bosnia and Croatia with the help of the UNHCR since the signing of the Dayton peace accords in 1995.
NASA BORBA
- Democratic Party announces start of anti-election campaign from August 21 until presidential and parliamentary elections on September 21 throughout Serbia.
- Without foreign observers participation in Serbian elections senseless, says independent trade unions organisation Nezavisnost.

- War crimes prosecutor Louise Arbour has announced a visit to Montenegro in September to establish the responsibility of Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic for events on the Dubrovnik front in 1992.
- Under new draft law owners of hard currency accounts frozen since 1991 will be able to choose between purchasing shares in folded Yugoslav firms or waiting 13 years to withdraw their savings.
BORBA
- Supply of meat and meat products on the market normalising after state intervention from reserves, said Serbian Trade Minister Srdjan Nikolic.
- Bor copper mining and smelting complex exported more than 6,500 tonnes of finished copper products in the first seven months of the year, or 55 percent of total production.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA
- Republican election commission confirms Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic as Democratic Party of Socialists of Montenegro presidential candidate for October elections.

- Italy to open consular office in Bar in September, said Montenegrin Foreign Minister Branko Perovic. Greece has initiated a procedure to open a consular office and Russia might do the same. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
